findings.summary: The test-data figures (0 meets Post on 97.7-100%, median |attnRef| 0.009-0.04, p's fp8 rounding >= |attnRef| on 81-100%) do not hold at test_op's N_CTX = 128, the last not at 1024 either
findings.detail: Specification, 'Where Post does not tell o from 0', first bullet, says of 'every shape of test_op' that 0 meets Post on 97.7% to 100% of the sampled elements, that |attnRef| has median 0.009 to 0.04, and that p's fp8 rounding alone, sum p*|v| / (8 sum p), is at least |attnRef| on 81% to 100% of them; Narrowings ('The tolerances' form') repeats the 97.7% and says 'On the test's data that is the fp8 rounding of p itself'. Evaluating Model.lean's tolO and tolV row by row on the test's data (normal(0, 0.5) through float16 to float8e5, sm_scale = 0.5, one head with vIn, every row at N_CTX = 128, three seeds; work/tolerance.out), these hold at N_CTX = 4096 but not at test_op's N_CTX = 128: there 0 meets Post on 87% to 89% of the elements at HEAD_DIM = 64 causal (the rejections are tolO's, not tolV's), the median |attnRef| is 0.044 to 0.094, and p's fp8 rounding alone is at least |attnRef| on only 26% to 54% of the elements (58% to 95% at N_CTX = 1024). So at N_CTX = 128 a bound with only p's fp8 rounding would reject 0 on about half or more of the elements, where Post rejects at most 13%: there the gap is mostly the library's constants (pE about 1.1 to 1.6 and psiA), not the fp8 format. Suggested: give the figures per N_CTX (or restrict them to the sizes they hold at) and say in Narrowings that at the test's smallest N_CTX most of the gap is Num.DotE5m2's. The conclusion (on the test's data Post does not tell o from 0) stands at every shape.
findings.evidence: work/tolerance.py and work/tolerance.out: the 'test' rows at N = 128 and 1024 and the 'test all' rows (three seeds); column p8 is the share with sum w|v| / (8 sum w) >= |attnRef|

findings.summary: Say plainly that tolV accepts every output within the range of the row's own values, whatever q, k, sm_scale (tolV >= 9/8*K + |attnRef|/8 at every nblk): alone it checks the key set, not the weights
findings.detail: The README calls tolV 'a magnitude bound' and says the weighted mean 'can lie almost anywhere between the row's values'. The exact content is simpler and worth one sentence: magA's second branch gives magA >= magCp > 9/8*K + |attnRef|/8 (rho8 > 0), so tolV >= 9/8*K + |attnRef|/8 at every nblk (work/tolerance.out, the hull margin column: at least 0.16*|attnRef| at nblk = 1). Every average c of the row's own values v[bh, j, e], j in keys d n, with any nonnegative weights has |c - attnRef| <= K, and its float8e5 rounding is within K + (K + |attnRef|)/8 + 2^-17 of attnRef, below tolV (whose 2^-17 term is the same). So the tolV clause is met by, for example, the plain mean of the row's values, or v[bh, j, e] for any one key j, whatever q, k and sm_scale: by itself it checks that the output lies in (a widening of) the range of the values of the row's keys, which pins the key set (the causal mask) and the range, and the weights only through tolO. That is also why it rejects 0 only when the row's values sit close to attnRef. Not a doubt of the bound; Mag.lane_E and Mag.estep_real compare acc with r*l_i over the computed p, as the README says.
findings.evidence: work/tolerance.py and work/tolerance.out (the a_T, b_T and hull-margin table); Model.lean's magCp, magNext, tolV

release.note: Resolved as round 1 asked under (b), and more: the README now says plainly, in Specification ('Where Post does not tell o from 0') and in Narrowings, that on the test's and the benchmark's data and on rows spread over many blocks Post accepts o = 0, names the causes (p's fp8 rounding, Num.DotE5m2's pE and compounding, L124), and 'meaningful on the test's shapes and data' is gone; the Post docstring says neither tolerance need be below |attnRef|. The new tolV (definitions printed in work/axioms.out, formulas re-run in work/tolerance.py) is what the README says, and it adds real content: about 6.6 instead of 1.4e4 on the benchmark at D = 128, N = 1024, and +-0 pinned for the heads without vIn at every covered size (2^-17; tolO alone allowed 9.2e-4 at D = 256, N = 2^16). The remaining errors in the README's test-data figures are a new DOC.

Referred to library issue L124, which states the request as raised (the compounding of relDot8 64 on |acc|, the score's relDot8 D inside the exponent, and the suggested per-instruction form); it is tracked there.

Done: kernel.json's title (listed in kernels/README.md), the README's opening ('Read this first'), the kernel paragraph and the root module's docstring now say that only the first ceil(Z*H/HEAD_DIM) heads read v and every other head outputs +-0, and the opening gives the host's count (all but 1 to 3 heads).

notes: Round 2 re-read item:spec at its new digest (the only changed item): Post's new clause, tolV, magA, magD, magNext, magCp as Lean elaborates them (work/axioms.out), and the statements of Mag (lminB, lmin_real, p_big, lane_pq, lane_E, estep_real, final_v), Row.RowSt and Row.mag_tail, Step.astep's added conjunct, RowMax.mstep_* and Program.row_out. main, consistent and satisfiable still use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. work/tolerance.py transcribes tolV from Model.lean (K the smallest bound Post allows, max_j |vEff_j - attnRef| over the row's keys) and reproduces the README's tolV figures: 0.644, 1.13, 2.55, 71 and 1.13e7 for q = 0, v = 1 at N = 1024 to 2^16; 6.64 and 6.69 on the benchmark's data at N = 1024 (README 6.5, 6.7); 360 and 359 at 2^14 (README 358, 351); 144 and 145 on test-like data at 2^14; tolV / |attnRef| = 0.308 for one key; 7.6e-6 for vEff = 0; tolV < |attnRef| needs K below 0.529*|attnRef| at 2 blocks and 0.217 at 16, never from 31 blocks on (README: 0.53, 0.22, never from 32 on).
